name: Vanguard (Orphaned Bookworm Productions)
body:
The vanguard is the master of the battlefield as well as a low member of high society. A protector of allies and a bastion of hope, they are first to charge and last to fall in defense of those to whom they are sworn.

Depending on the culture a vanguard may be known by other names in order to suit your campaign. Options include but are not limited to, knight, chevalier, ritter, bushi, sohei or other title that implies officer or leadership roles in an army or other organized fighting force, typically those with some political or social standing, no matter how small.

Why Vanguard and not Knight?: When designing the class and looking back at its inspiration, we decided against retaining the name for a couple of reasons. First, the knight carries a lot of baggage, both as a reference to the older class and its cultural implications in the crusades.

Second, we did not want to pigeonhole the class to only Euro-centric characters when the options would be available to similar warriors from various cultures and backgrounds.

Class Details

Role: The vanguard is a competent melee combatant but excels at protecting themselves and their allies from harm. They inspire their companions and provoke their enemies. None can match the vanguard’s control of the battlefield.

Alignment: Any lawful. A vanguard need not be good, but they need to be able to dedicate themselves fully to an oath and respect authority they view as legitimate. Neutral and evil vanguards tend to be literalists when it comes to their oaths and an evil vanguard may lose respect for any authority they see as weak, given time. Good vanguards often keep their word in spirit rather than the letter alone and swear oaths they believe will serve good ends.

Hit Die: d12

Starting Wealth: 5d6 x 10 (175 gp). In addition, each character begins play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less.

Level	Base Attack Bonus	Fort Save	Ref Save	Will Save	Features
1st	+1	+2	+0	+2	Code of honor, fighter training, test of valor, valorous deflection
2nd	+2	+3	+0	+3	Aristocratic training, shield focus (+1), weapons of the guardian
3rd	+3	+3	+1	+3	Armor Training, behind me
4th	+4	+4	+1	+4	Trial by combat
5th	+5	+4	+1	+4	Ever vigilant, uncanny dodge
6th	+6/+1	+5	+2	+5	Active defense (CMD, Touch AC), combat feat
7th	+7/+2	+5	+2	+5	Always ready, armor training, press the advantage, weapons of guardian
8th	+8/+3	+6	+2	+6	Call to action, shield focus (+2)
9th	+9/+4	+6	+3	+6	Brace, bulwark, improved uncanny dodge
10th	+10/+5	+7	+3	+7	Combat feat, indomitable determination, stalwart
11th	+11/+6/+1	+7	+3	+7	Active defense (ally, Ref), armor training, death before dishonor
12th	+12/+7/+2	+8	+4	+8	Bring ’em down, improved press the advantage, weapons of the guardian
13th	+13/+8/+3	+8	+4	+8	Always ready (3), to arms
14th	+14/+9/+4	+9	+4	+9	Combat feat, implacable, shield focus (+3)
15th	+15/+10/+5	+9	+5	+9	Armor Training, truly indomitable
16th	+16/+11/+6/+1	+10	+5	+10	Active defense (constant, two allies), overwhelming presence
17th	+17/+12/+7/+2	+10	+5	+10	Incredible recovery
18th	+18/+13/+8/+3	+11	+6	+11	Always ready (4), combat feat, unstoppable
19th	+19/+14/+9/+4	+11	+6	+11	Second skin
20th	+20/+15/+10/+5	+12	+6	+12	Protector of the realm, shield focus (+4)
Class Skills

The vanguard’s class skills are: Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Handle Animal (Cha), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (local) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Survival (Wis), and Swim (Str).

Skill Ranks per Level: 4 + Int modifier

Class Features

The following are the class features of the vanguard.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

A vanguard is proficient with all simple and martial weapons and with all armor (heavy, light, and medium) and shields (including tower shields).

Code of Honor

To maintain faith in themselves and the faith of their allies the vanguard must adhere to a short but strict list of rules.

Never strike a helpless foe with lethal damage.
Allow enemies to ready themselves before striking. The vanguard never benefits from a foe being flat-footed.
The vanguard’s word is their bond. The vanguard must uphold any promises or oaths they swear.
Honor freely given surrender and allow parley if possible.

If the vanguard breaks any of these rules they lose a point of Mettle and their maximum Mettle pool is reduced by one until 24 hours have passed for each time they have broken this code. These effects are cumulative. This is a result of having shaken their own pride and faith in themselves by resorting to underhanded tactics.

Fighter Training

The vanguard’s class levels count as fighter levels for the purposes of prerequisites.

Mettle (Ex)

Many of the vanguard’s abilities are powered by a resource called Mettle. This is a representation of their devotion to personal honor, oaths, and determination.

At 1st level, the vanguard gains a pool of Mettle that is refreshed each day. The pool’s maximum is equal to the vanguard’s Charisma modifier, plus any feats and special abilities that increases the pool maximum. Some abilities may restore points to this pool during the day.

But the vanguard may not have more points of Mettle than the pool’s maximum.

The vanguard may expend Mettle to gain one of the following benefits.

As an immediate action the vanguard may gain a bonus equal to their Charisma modifier on the next saving throw. The bonus must be used before the beginning of their next turn.
As part of making a Strength or Dexterity check to gain a bonus equal to their Charisma bonus on that check. The vanguard may restore a point of Mettle to your pool in the following ways.
If the vanguard uses the aid another action to assist an ally’s skill check and the ally would have failed the check without the vanguard’s action

Example: If the vanguard use the aid another action on an ally climbing a rope (DC 10) and the ally rolls an 8, with the vanguard’s aid another this brings the ally’s roll to 10 which is enough to succeed and would restore a point of Mettle to the vanguard’s pool.

If the vanguard uses the aid another action to improve an ally’s AC and the ally would have been hit without the vanguard’s action
If the target of the vanguard’s test of valor is a creature with a CR equal to the vanguard’s Character Level +2 and they are victorious in the encounter without falling unconscious.

If an ability which expends Mettle allows for the use of an attack of opportunity, the attack of opportunity allowed by that ability may be taken even while using the total defense action.

Test of Valor (Ex)

At 1st level, the vanguard expends a point of Mettle to issue a challenge as a free action to any creature that has an Intelligence score of 5 or greater. It must be intelligent enough to have a sense of pride, honor, and/or narcissism. It need not share a language with the vanguard, as many creatures can understand a challenge and recognize a threat. This creature must be of a CR no less than the vanguard’s character level – 2.

While this challenge lasts, the vanguard gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls, and damage rolls. At 5th level and every 5 levels thereafter these bonuses each increase by an additional +1.

The test of valor lasts until the vanguard or the target falls to 0 or fewer hit points or combat ends because either the vanguard or the target have surrendered honestly.

If a cowardly knave surrenders as a trick, the vanguard does not need to spend another point of Mettle to regain the bonuses of the effect. The challenge resumes with renewed fervor because the target has attempted to take advantage of your honor or reputation. When this happens the bonuses from the original challenge are doubled. This automatic regaining of your test of valor bonuses can only occur within the first hour after combat ends.

Valorous Deflection (Ex)

At 1st level, when an opponent makes a melee attack against the vanguard or an adjacent ally, they can spend a point of Mettle and a use of an attack of opportunity to attempt to parry the attack. The vanguard makes an attack roll as if they were making an attack of opportunity. For each size category the attacking creature is larger, the vanguard takes a -2 penalty to this attack. If the attempt is made using a shield attack, the vanguard may apply any enhancement or ability bonuses to shield AC to the attack. If the attack result is greater than the attackers, the attack automatically misses. The attempt must be declared before the results of the attack are known.

If this attack is made while the vanguard is using the Combat Expertise feat, fighting defensively, or taking the total defense action they may also add the bonus from those abilities to the attack roll to block an attack, but loses any used bonuses until the beginning of their next turn.

Upon a successful parry, if the vanguard has at least one point of Mettle they may make a riposte attack on the creature they parried as an immediate action, provided the target is in the vanguard’s threatened area. If the parry attempt fails, the attack is instead directed at the vanguard at its normal result and the vanguard is flatfooted and loses their shield bonus to AC if the shield was used in the attempt.

Aristocratic Training (Ex)

The vanguard’s training includes the skills needed to understand the lives of dignitaries and nobles. At 2nd level, the vanguard gains a bonus equal to 1/2 their vanguard class levels on Diplomacy, Knowledge (nobility), and Sense Motive checks. Additionally, this allows the vanguard to make Knowledge (nobility) checks untrained without the maximum result of 10.

Shield Focus (Ex)

The vanguard is a master of defense. At 2nd level, the vanguard gains Shield Focus as a bonus feat. At 8th level and every 6 levels thereafter the bonus granted by the Shield Focus feat increases by an additional +1. They only receive this additional benefit on one wielded shield.

Weapons of the Guardian (Ex)

At 2nd level, the vanguard gains Improved Shield Bash and Two-Weapon Fighting as bonus feats. Additionally, the vanguard may treat heavy shields as light weapons for the purposes of two-weapon fighting penalties as long as they wield only one shield.

At 7th level, the vanguard gains Improved Two-Weapon Fighting and at 12th level, they gain Greater Two-Weapon Fighting as bonus feats. They do not need to meet the prerequisites for these bonus feats, though these feats only apply when wielding a shield in one hand.

Armor Training (Ex)

Starting at 3rd level, a vanguard learns to be more maneuverable while wearing armor. Whenever they are wearing armor, they reduce the armor check penalty by 1 (to a minimum of 0) and increases the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed by their armor by 1. Every four levels thereafter (7th, 11th, and 15th), these bonuses increase by +1 each time, to a maximum –4 reduction of the armor check penalty and a +4 increase of the maximum Dexterity bonus allowed.

Additionally, the vanguard can also move at their normal speed while wearing medium armor. At 7th level, the vanguard can move at his normal speed while wearing heavy armor.

Advanced Armor Training: At 7th level, instead of increasing the benefits provided by armor training (reducing their armor’s check penalty by 1 and increasing its max Dex bonus by 1), the vanguard can choose an advanced armor training option available to the fighter. If the vanguard does so, they still gain the ability to move at their normal speed while wearing heavy armor at 7th level.

Behind Me (Ex)

At 3rd level, the vanguard may elect to place themselves in the path of danger in order to protect an ally. When rolling initiative, the vanguard may select a target as a charge. This selection may not change for the duration of the encounter. Any time that the vanguard is within 5 feet of their charge, and the charge is the target of an attack, the vanguard may, as an immediate action, enter the square occupied by the charge and receive the attack in their place. The attack automatically hits the vanguard. The charge is placed in any empty square adjacent to the vanguard of the vanguard’s choice. The vanguard may declare the use of this ability after knowing whether their charge will be hit.

If the vanguard suffers a critical hit as a result of using behind me they restore a point of Mettle.

Trial by Combat (Ex)

At 4th level, the vanguard can shout a challenge to all enemies within 100 feet that can both see and hear the vanguard as a standard action.

This appeals to the enemy’s pride, narcissism, fear, anger or other emotions and paints the vanguard as a threat to be vanquished. This only affects enemies who would be subject to the vanguard’s test of valor ability and expends a point of Mettle to activate. Each enemy to be affected must make a Will save equal to 10 + 1/2 the vanguard’s class level + their Charisma modifier.

Each enemy that fails must attack the vanguard or include the vanguard in the area of effect of a spell or special ability that doesn’t target creatures.

An enemy under the effects of trial by combat can choose not to attack vanguard and instead spend a standard action calming their emotions and rolling a new save. Otherwise, trial by combat lasts for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the vanguard’s class levels + their Charisma modifier.

If the vanguard is rendered unconscious by damage taken from targets under the effect of trial by combat, the vanguard restores two points of Mettle.

Ever Vigilant (Ex)

At 5th level, all squares the vanguard threatens with a melee weapon, including just a shield, are considered difficult terrain for enemies.

This ability applies even to jumping, flying, and incorporeal foes, as well as swarms, so long as the vanguard wields a melee weapon or shield capable of affecting them. The vanguard must be aware of the enemy to affect them.

The vanguard also provides cover but not total cover to adjacent allies if the vanguard’s square lies between the ally and the origin of the attack or effect that includes the ally as a target.

Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 5th level, a vanguard gains the ability to react to danger before their senses would normally allow them to do so. They cannot be caught flat-footed, nor do they lose their Dex bonus to AC if the attacker is invisible. They still lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if immobilized. A vanguard with this ability can still lose their Dexterity bonus to armor class if an opponent successfully uses the feint action against them. If a vanguard already has uncanny dodge from a different class, they automatically gain improved uncanny dodge (see page 5) instead.

Active Defense (Ex)

At 6th level, the vanguard may spend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to apply any shield bonus they benefit from to their CMD and touch AC for a number of rounds equal to their Charisma modifier. The vanguard may activate this ability even while grappled or otherwise restrained so long as they are still benefiting from a shield bonus.

Starting at 11th level, the vanguard may apply this bonus to themselves and one adjacent ally.

Additionally, this ability now adds the vanguard’s shield bonus to Reflex saves during duration.

Starting at 16th level, the vanguard’s shield bonus always applies to their own CMD, touch AC and Reflex saving throws. The vanguard may now expend a use of Mettle to apply this bonus to up to two adjacent allies.

Combat Feat

At 6th level, the vanguard gains a bonus combat feat for which they meet the prerequisites.

They gain additional bonus combat feats at 10th, 14th, and 18th levels.

Press the Advantage (Ex)

At 7th level, the vanguard gains the ability to make a special shield bash as either a standard action or at the end of a charge. If this attack hits it deals damage as though the vanguard was wielding a shield one size category larger. Also, until the beginning of the vanguard’s next turn the target takes a penalty to their AC equal to the vanguard’s Charisma bonus as their defenses are thrown open by the surprising assault and the vanguard’s daunting presence.

Always Ready (Ex)

At 7th level, whenever the vanguard rolls for initiative they gain 2 bonus points of Mettle that exceeds their normal maximum. This Mettle is spent first if the vanguard uses any abilities which require Mettle. If the vanguard spends no Mettle before the end of combat these bonus points disappear when combat ends. The bonus points of Mettle gained increases to 3 at 13th level and to 4 at 19th level.

Damage Reduction (Ex)

At 7th level, the vanguard gains DR 1/-. This damage reduction improves by 1 at 11th level and every four levels thereafter.

Call to Action (Ex)

At 8th level, the vanguard gains the ability to rouse the minds and bodies of their allies.

By spending a point of Mettle as a move action the vanguard can shout a word of encouragement and inspiration to their allies. All allies within 100 feet that can see and hear the vanguard may immediately make a new saving throw against any mind-affecting ability, ability that impedes their movement, or ability that limits the kinds of actions they can take on their turn (this also grants a new check to escape a grapple, though this isn’t a saving throw). The ally gains a bonus on this new roll equal to the vanguard’s Charisma bonus. If this new roll is successful the effect is treated as though the ally had succeeded on their original save.

The vanguard regains an amount of Mettle equal to the number of allies who succeeded their check or save, up to their Charisma modifier.

Bulwark (Ex)

At 9th level, the vanguard has learned to defend against some kinds of magic. If they are armored or wielding a shield they may expend a point of Mettle and deflect a ray effect that targets them as an immediate action causing it to harmlessly dissipate.

If the vanguard expends an additional point of Mettle they make a Reflex save against that ray using whatever the save DC vs the effect would normally be, even if it does not allow one. If the vanguard succeeds they may redirect the ray to a target of their choice. The target must be within range of the spell as though the vanguard was the point of origin. This redirection uses the same attack roll result by the original caster.

Brace (Ex)

At 9th level, if the vanguard succeeds on a Reflex save against a spell or effect while wielding a shield they may expend a point of Mettle as an immediate action to prevent that effect from affecting all squares adjacent to them as well as negating the effect fully on the vanguard.

Improved Uncanny Dodge (Ex)

At 9th level, a vanguard can no longer be flanked. This defense denies a n enemy the ability to sneak attack the vanguard by flanking them, unless the attacker has at least four more sneak-attack class levels than the vanguard’s class levels.

If a character already has uncanny dodge from another class, the levels from the classes that grant uncanny dodge stack to determine the minimum sneak attack level required to flank the vanguard.

Stalwart (Ex)

At 10th level, if the vanguard succeeds at a Fortitude or Will save against an effect that would have a partial effect on a successful save they instead suffer no effects.

Indomitable Determination (Ex)

At 10th level, the vanguard gains the following for use with Mettle.

When the vanguard spends Mettle to add their Charisma bonus to a Strength or Dexterity check the vanguard also halves the DC of that check.
The vanguard may spend a point of Mettle to remove the fatigued, shaken, or sickened condition from themselves as a free action on their turn, but no more than once each round.
Death Before Dishonor (Ex)

At 11th level, the vanguard gains Diehard as a bonus feat without needing to meet the prerequisites. At any time while the Diehard feat is active, the vanguard may expend a point of Mettle to suppress the staggered condition for the round. Any strenuous action still causes damage as normal.

Additionally, if the vanguard’s hit points are below their Constitution score, they may expend a point of Mettle each round to continue to act under the Diehard feat until they reach a negative hp total equal to their vanguard class levels plus their Constitution score. During this time, the vanguard may still expend additional Mettle to suppress the staggered condition.

If the vanguard does not expend Mettle while still within this threshold, they are considered dying and stable for one round. If they do not receive healing within the round to bring their hit points back above their Constitution score, they die.

Bring ‘em Down (Ex)

At 12th level, the vanguard is able to defend their immediate area against all who would attempt to force their way by.

As long as the vanguard has a point of mettle they may make attacks of opportunity against foes that enter their threatened area even if under the effect of a spell or ability that otherwise prevents attacks of opportunity such as Flyby Attack or Improved Grapple. If this attack hits, the vanguard may expend a point of Mettle to deal damage as normal and if the attack roll would also beat the target’s CMD, they are tripped. This ability allows the vanguard to trip flying creatures. A flying creature tripped by this ability falls to the ground.

The vanguard may spend 2 points of Mettle when making this attack to resolve against the lower of the target’s AC or CMD. The target is dazed for 1 round it succeeds at a Fortitude saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + 1/2 the vanguard’s class level + the vanguard’s Charisma modifier.

Improved Press the Advantage (Ex)

At 12th level, whenever the vanguard hits with press the advantage, they may make a free bull rush attempt against the target without provoking an attack of opportunity and a bonus on this attempt equal to half the damage originally dealt. Additionally, they are not limited in the distance they can push the target based on the vanguard’s movement for the round, they are only limited by the distance the bull rush maneuver would allow to the target to be pushed. otherwise this follows the basic bull rush rules. These movements provoke attacks of opportunity from creatures other than vanguard or the subjects of the bull rush. If the target(s) are pushed into a solid object or an additional creature the vanguard is unable to move, any creature pushed into it takes 1d6 for each 10ft they were pushed, plus the vanguard’s Strength modifier. The same amount of damage is dealt to the object or creature which halted the bull rush.

To Arms (Ex)

At 13th level, the vanguard has learned to truly lead by example. As a full-round action that costs 2 points of Mettle, the vanguard may make a single attack against an enemy. If it hits, this attack is treated as the feat Vital Strike, and each ally within 60 feet who can see and hear you is granted an attack of opportunity on a target they threaten or a target within the first range increment of a ranged or thrown weapon they are currently wielding. This ability allows allies with ranged weapons to make an attack of opportunity when they normally could not. This ability benefits from the Improved Vital Strike and better feats.

Implacable (Ex)

At 14th level, the vanguard is no longer slowed by difficult terrain, whether natural, magical, or magically augmented.

Additionally, the vanguard is not slowed by effects which reduce their base move speed, and become immune to the dazed and stunned conditions so long as they have at least 1 point of Mettle and remain conscious.

Truly Indomitable (Ex)

At 15th level, the vanguard adds exhausted, frightened, panicked, and nauseated to the conditions they may remove with indomitable determination, though removing these conditions costs 2 points of Mettle instead of 1.

Overwhelming Presence (Ex)

At 16th level, as a swift action the vanguard may spend 2 points of Mettle to project their superior skill and strength of arms to all enemies, weeding out the weak and allowing only the strong to face them. All enemies within 60 feet of the vanguard must make a Will save (DC equal to 10 + 1/2 the vanguard’s class levels + the vanguard’s Charisma modifier) or become shaken until the end of combat.

Any creature that fails its save by 5 or more or has fewer HD than the vanguard’s character level minus 4 is frightened for 1 minute. Afterwards they become shaken as long as they can see and hear the vanguard.

Regardless of the outcome, this ability can only affect a given creature once every 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting fear effect, though it can affect any creature with an Intelligence score regardless of immunity, in such a case the creature can only become shaken.

Incredible Recovery (Ex)

At 17th level, the vanguard’s ability to recover from injury is truly extraordinary. They gain fast healing 1 when not in combat. This cannot restore hit points lost to starvation, thirst, or suffocation nor does it reattach severed limbs.

Unstoppable (Ex)

At 18th level, while the vanguard has at least 3 points of Mettle and is conscious they are immune to the entangled, grappled, pinned, petrified, and paralyzed conditions.

Second Skin (Ex)

At 19th level, whenever the vanguard is wearing armor or wielding a shield their damage reduction class feature improves to DR 5/- and stacks with any damage reduction gained from their armor or shield.

Protector of the Realm (Su)

The vanguard has, across their many battles, learned to face hardships beyond what most would bear. The vanguard’s unwavering devotion to their ideals and their allies manifests as a reputation that always precedes them.

The vanguard is known far and wide as someone who would never falter, never break their oaths, and never simply allow an ally to fall.

At 20th level, the vanguard gains an aura of law as a cleric of the same level. Any weapon they wield is treated as lawfully-aligned, people of lawful alignments always have a starting attitude of at least indifferent to the vanguard unless they have been given direct orders to oppose the vanguard and their allies, and lastly, they no longer need to expend Mettle to activate test of valor, behind me!, and trial by combat, these abilities only require the vanguard to spend the action the ability requires.
